item.text: {"text":"Recent work distinguishes relatedness from functional complementarity: the [TREC 2025 track overview, published in 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17138), explicitly separates complementary and related products; [ECCR (2024)](https://genai-personalization.github.io/assets/papers/GenAIRecP2024/Li.pdf) addresses incompatible complementary recommendations. These distinctions suggest separate diagnostic labels for thematic overlap, shared product identity, and explicitly supported compatibility. Using only titles/descriptions, record matching evidence spans and model identifiers; shared terminology alone cannot establish compatibility. Mark insufficient evidence as “unknown,” reserving “incompatible” for explicit contradictions.\n\nA [2026 user study of news recommendations](https://doi.org/10.1145/3808221) measures relevance, satisfaction, selection, and adoption separately, illustrating why textual similarity cannot stand in for purchase intent. Practical proxies here could include exact repeated IDs, possible near-duplicate titles with preserved edition/model differences, and overlap with recent versus older history. These are proposed diagnostics, not validated intent measures: timestamps establish recency, not loss of interest. Validate each proxy against available explicit feedback, reporting labeled counts and uncertainty; absent feedback means validation remains unavailable. The [2025 abstention survey](https://aclanthology.org/2025.tacl-1.26/) supports withholding unsupported judgments, but supplies no ready-made threshold for this setting. Report evidence coverage alongside diagnostic rates, retain macro validation HR@10 for model selection, and treat simulator feedback as distinct from observed human feedback."}
